subject: Ventosol dedicated pool: safety curve, compute allocation & latency targets
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@ventosol.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial demand sheet + latency target for Ventosol campaign

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is our current demand profile (ventosol_demand_profile.xlsx) for the April marketing push. High level: we expect two main traffic waves — a daytime steady-state and a short multi-hour campaign spike. Key asks we need to validate before we sign a dedicated commitment:

- Confirm tokens/sec per GPU estimate for rw-large-v2 (quantized) with 2k-context at 512 avg tokens/call.
- Recommend safety buffer to hit 300ms p95 for generation endpoints (no heavy tool calls).
- Advice on burst strategy (reserved pool vs autoscale buffer) and any impact on per-token unit economics.

Traffic snapshots in the sheet: peak tokens/sec (preliminary) ~ 120k t/s for the campaign hour; baseline ~ 18k t/s. We're open to proposals that reduce cost while meeting latency targets (e.g., model fallbacks, prefilling caches).

Can you do an initial sizing and outline next steps for a short Pilot?

Best,
Olivia Park
Head of Platform
Vent0 Solutions

Thanks Olivia — received the sheet and good summary. Looping in Karthik (inference capacity modeling) and Marissa (account lead) to align on commercial fit.

High-level plan from our side:
- I will run a tokens/sec -> GPU conversion with two scenarios: (A) steady-state + burst buffer, (B) aggressive safety-curve (30% headroom) to guarantee p95 targets.
- Karthik will validate assumptions on cache hit-rate, quantization uplift, and expected token throughput for rw-large-v2 on A100/NVIDIA H100 variants.
- We need a clarified p95/p99 requirement (you mentioned 300ms p95). Also confirm avg tokens per call (sheet lists 512, please confirm distribution).

Quick asks to unblock a tight sizing:
1) Confirm p99 target (not just p95).
2) Are you okay with a staged commit: pilot on a 4-GPU reserved slab with a 2x burst buffer, then scale to the full slab if metrics hold?
3) Any regulatory constraints (data residency) that would push us to a specific region?

I'll come back with a first-cut estimate by EOD tomorrow.

— Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Quick clarifications:
- p95 = 300ms is firm for the pilot. p99 we can tolerate up to 600ms for this run (we'll flag degraded experiences).
- Average tokens per call we expect to be ~420 (distribution attached in the updated sheet). Peak concurrent active sessions estimate ~8.5k during the campaign hour.
- No special residency constraints — US region is fine.
- Pilot staging OK to start with 4 GPUs + burst; if you recommend >4 for safety, recommend options.

Thanks,
Olivia

On a related note: we prefer a solver that accounts for cache warmup and cold-starts because our app frequently creates new chat sessions that bypass prefix caching for the first turn.
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@ventosol.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial demand sheet + latency target for Ventosol campaign

Olivia/Jonas — dug into the numbers and sketched the throughput math. Attaching a PDF with the notebook snippets (jw-vento-compute-notes.pdf). Key points below.

Assumptions we used:
- Model: rw-large-v2 quantized (int8) on A100/80GB equivalent.
- Measured steady-state throughput per A100 (512-token avg, 2k context): ~6.8k tokens/sec under continuous batching at 20 concurrent streams; p95 latency ~180–220ms in our bench.
- KV/prefix cache hit-rate: 0.35 baseline; when first-turns dominate, effective tokens/sec capacity drops ~22–28% (more decode work, less cache reuse).

Sizing math (peak snapshot):
- Ventosol peak tokens/sec input (campaign hour): 120k t/s (sheet).
- Effective per-GPU capacity accounting for reduced cache hit-rate: assume 6.8k * 0.75 = ~5.1k t/s per A100 equivalent.
- Required GPUs = ceil(120k / 5.1k) = ~24 GPUs to sustain the peak if we serve only rw-large-v2.

Mitigations and recommended safety curve:
1) Safety headroom: add 30% buffer for microbursts and cold-session churn => 24 * 1.3 = ~31 GPU-equivalents.
2) Cost-saving hybrid: reserve 16 GPUs for steady-state + 8 GPU burst slab (on-demand or pre-warmed) + model-fallback lane (smaller variant rw-medium) to shed load beyond 24 GPUs. This hits your 300ms p95 in most cases while cutting committed spend by ~40%.
3) Autoscale latency tail: pre-warm KV caches on expected campaign cohorts, and enable shorter TTLs for cold sessions to reduce first-turn cost.
4) Ops playbook: circuit-breaker at 28 GPU-equivalents, degrade gracefully to rw-medium for non-critical endpoints.

Tradeoffs: committed slab of 31 GPUs guarantees coverage but is expensive. Hybrid reserved+burst with fallbacks achieves 95% of availability at materially lower cost. We'll provide a cost comparison (attached) and a short-run pilot config to validate p95 under realistic session churn.

Next steps: Jonas — if Ventosol signs pilot, we'll provision a 16-GPU reserved pool + 8-GPU warm burst for the first week and run a stress test with synthetic traffic sampled from their sheet. If p95 < 300ms at 90% of runs, scale commit up per the action plan below.

— Karthik
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial demand sheet + latency target for Ventosol campaign — proposal and MAP

Olivia — summarizing the recommendation and proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP):

Recommendation summary (condensed)
- Pilot configuration: 16x A100-equivalent reserved + 8x A100 warm-burst slab (pre-warmed), model: rw-large-v2 (quantized) + fallback rw-medium.
- Expected steady-state coverage: ~18k t/s baseline. Burst coverage: up to ~24k t/s with warm slab; to reach 120k t/s peak we'd rely on fallback shedding beyond 24 GPUs unless Ventosol expands the committed slab.
- Safety curve: plan for a 30% headroom (operational threshold at ~28–31 GPU-equivalents).
- SLOs: target p95 <= 300ms (pilot) and p99 <= 600ms (acceptable). We'll instrument token-level tracing to validate.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP)
1) By 2028-03-28: Ventosol confirms pilot sign-off and provides final traffic CSV (Jonas).
2) 2028-03-29 to 2028-04-02: Redwood provisions reserved 16 GPU pool + 8 GPU warm slab, seeds KV cache with synthetic sessions (Karthik).
3) 2028-04-03: Run ramp test (synthetic) and 2-hour live campaign dry-run; collect p95/p99 and token throughput metrics (joint).
4) 2028-04-05: Review results, decide on commit scale-up (options: expand committed slab to 31 GPUs or accept hybrid fallback strategy).

Commercial notes: Marissa will follow up on pricing for (a) 16+8 hybrid pilot, (b) all-reserved 31-GPU commitment, and (c) per-hour burst pricing. Marissa, please attach the cost comparison and the DocuSign link when ready.

If this looks good Olivia, we can kick the provisioning as soon as we get your final CSV and the formal pilot sign-off.

— Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
